questions.prompt: What should a region containing one grid cell become?

choices.label: A leaf containing that cell’s value.
choices.feedback: One cell already has one uniform value, so it needs no smaller regions.

choices.label: A leaf whose value is always one.
choices.feedback: One cell already has one uniform value, so it needs no smaller regions.

choices.label: An internal node with four empty children.
choices.feedback: One cell already has one uniform value, so it needs no smaller regions.

questions.prompt: How should a larger square be divided for recursion?

choices.label: Into overlapping squares around each cell.
choices.feedback: Halving the side length creates the four nonoverlapping quadrants represented by a quad-tree node.

choices.label: Into two unequal strips.
choices.feedback: Halving the side length creates the four nonoverlapping quadrants represented by a quad-tree node.

choices.label: Into four equal square quadrants.
choices.feedback: Halving the side length creates the four nonoverlapping quadrants represented by a quad-tree node.

questions.prompt: When can the four child nodes be replaced by one leaf?

choices.label: When any two children have the same value.
choices.feedback: Only four equal-valued leaves prove that every cell in the entire region has the same value.

choices.label: When the four children have equal sizes.
choices.feedback: Only four equal-valued leaves prove that every cell in the entire region has the same value.

choices.label: When all four are leaves with the same value.
choices.feedback: Only four equal-valued leaves prove that every cell in the entire region has the same value.
